correctness.rationale: For odd v and k=(v−1)/2, normalized Fourier transform has nonprincipal square mass (v−1)c² with c=sqrt(v+1)/(2v). The identity sum(a−c)²=2c((v−1)c−sum a) gives the exact coefficient v/sqrt(v+1). The Fourier autocorrelation inversion proves equality iff off-zero difference multiplicity is (v−3)/4. A second Parseval identity V=v³ sum(a²−c²)² and 0<=a<=k/v yield the two explicit two-sided V bounds. Paley difference sets attain for prime v≡3 mod4; integrality and zero-sum deviations give V>=2 for any non-equality case. Independent all 126 halfsets in Z3×Z3 corroborate with maximal numerical identity residual <7e−16; finite check is NOT universal proof.
